rules: Open at second zero with the title's central conflict, promised action, or a specific revealing fact. No greeting, channel bumper, empty title card, or generic background introduction before the content.

Deliver a meaningful first answer, action, or piece of evidence within 10-15 seconds, earlier for a brief Short. A tease or a claim that something is amazing is not a payoff. Match the opening visuals and audio to the title and thumbnail's promise.

Remove loading, redundant travel, repeated explanations and empty pauses. Preserve setup, geography, natural phrasing and tension when they help the viewer understand the payoff. Do not force cuts at a fixed interval or replace storytelling with nonstop noise.

For gameplay highlights, prioritize original game dialogue and action sound. Default to natural game audio with no added narration or competing music. For documentaries and character lore, default to the exact approved Cedar voice preset in APPROVED_VOICE_PRESET.json. An explicit user choice, including a deliberately selected free-audio workflow, can override this default; record that choice.

Keep speech natural: no drunken trailer delivery, arbitrary pauses within phrases, post-production time stretching or pitch shifting. Rewrite or regenerate a line to fit. Keep dialogue centered and intelligible, duck supporting music, check clipping and mono compatibility. Stereo is not a claim of Atmos or surround certification.

Shorts must stand alone unless the user explicitly asks for a trailer or promotion. Finish the promised story within the requested runtime; do not append watch-the-full-video lines or long empty end cards.

Use the best available genuine footage. Record source identity and native/upload resolution, frame subjects appropriately for wide and vertical edits, label archival versus illustrative footage, and avoid artificial haze or lifted blacks. A 4K export does not make low-resolution footage native 4K.

Check factual claims, dates, names and casualty counts. Verify narration and caption pronunciation/alignment where possible. Distinguish reconstruction, interpretation and documented events. Do not invent events, quote attribution or factual certainty for a stronger hook.

Treat CTR, average percentage viewed, completion, and stayed-to-watch figures as context-dependent working benchmarks, never guaranteed promotion thresholds. APV is not completion rate. A fifteen-second average does not locate an exit at second fifteen. Six views cannot prove thumbnail success or an algorithmic clickbait penalty. Do not promise ten thousand or one million views.

Before delivery, inspect the opening thirty seconds, representative final frames and the actual promised payoff; check final duration, aspect ratio, caption framing, audio level, pronunciation and quiet gaps. Use retention curves and traffic sources, compared with similar uploads, to decide revisions. Report what was actually checked; self-reported plans and automated checks are not a human viewing/listening review.

GAMING STRATEGY: For gaming content, state a specific reason to watch beyond seeing the game played. Unless the user has already chosen a format, favor focused essays or practical guides for long-form and complete gameplay moments or insights for Shorts. Treat formats as hypotheses to test against comparable channel uploads; do not replace an explicitly requested highlight, full playthrough, review or other format.

GAMING ESSAYS: Build around one compelling question and a clear thesis about a mechanic, character, art inspiration, cultural context or other specific topic. Use observed gameplay and verified sources as evidence; develop an argument rather than merely narrating a plot recap or giving a generic verdict. Open on relevant evidence and deliver an initial answer within the existing payoff deadline. Use the approved Cedar narration for analysis and let original dialogue and action sound carry key scenes. Do not invent details about footage that has not been inspected.

GAMING GUIDES: For mechanics, glitches and speedruns, show the outcome at the opening, then teach reproducible inputs, prerequisites and steps. Verify the game version, platform and applicable category rules; distinguish a glitch demonstration from a valid submitted run. Verify time claims and current records against appropriate primary sources. Preserve uninterrupted proof where the claim requires it, and distinguish tutorial edits from an uncut run.

GAMING WALKTHROUGHS: Organize around searchable objectives, bosses, dungeons and item locations. Provide precise chapter timestamps checked against the final export. Remove loading, repeated attempts and redundant travel when they add no instructional value, while preserving route context and necessary steps. Do not label a guide 100 percent without verifying its stated completion scope. Do not cut an explicitly requested unedited run or full playthrough into a different format.

GAMING SHORTS: Deliver one complete feat, moment or insight with an immediate hook and the actual promised payoff. Pure gameplay highlights default to original game audio; narrated analysis uses Cedar. A Short must work independently and must not direct viewers to the long video unless the user requested a trailer or promotion. Do not show only a tease when the title promises a kill, finisher or result.

GAMING PLANNING AND EVIDENCE: In production_review.pacing_review, record the chosen format, specific viewer question or objective, footage or sources supporting the payoff, and relevant guide steps or chapter plan. Use content_type lore for narrated gaming essays, documentary for narrated instructional guides, and gameplay for original-audio highlights or unnarrated guides; select the matching existing audio default. These editorial instructions are reviewed against the actual content, not proven by automated text checks. Compare retention curves, sample size and traffic sources before changing strategy. Do not claim essays universally outperform Let's Plays or chapters guarantee reach. YouTube's reported 200 million video-essay views in 2024 covers all subjects, not gaming alone.

POLITICS MODE (production_review.mode = "politics"; default for civic, election and policy explainers): Tell the story through the coverage itself. Build the edit on genuine broadcast footage from named outlets chosen with the user (for example CNN, MS NOW, NBC, CBS, ABC, PBS), download each source at its native resolution, and keep a source manifest with outlet, programme, date, URL and the exact in/out points of every range shown.

POLITICS MODE EXCERPTS: Let people speak for themselves. Use short original-audio excerpts, each cut on word boundaries verified by a secondary transcription of the source window, starting and ending on a complete sentence or a complete question-and-answer pair, with about 0.1 s lead and 0.3 s tail. Every excerpt names its speaker, outlet and programme on screen; a speaker who is not identified by the source is attributed to the event, never guessed. Include the strongest answer from the other side (the official, the ally, the expert who disagrees with the critics) so the piece reports the argument rather than joins it.

POLITICS MODE FOOTAGE: All other footage is muted and labeled SOURCE FOOTAGE, MUTED with the outlet, programme and date under it. Never show the same source range twice within an export, and never replay a clip muted after it has played with sound; audit every seek against every other seek before rendering. Fox or other third-party clips that appear inside a source segment are labeled as re-broadcast by that source. Do not upscale; export at the sources' native resolution.

POLITICS MODE STRUCTURE: Open at second zero with the sharpest attributed line or the subject's own words; deliver the first hard number or document within fifteen seconds. Chapters open on a claim or question and are answered by an attributed excerpt, then narration that says who said it and what the public record supports. Numbers are attributed to the outlet or person who used them, illustrative arithmetic is labeled illustrative, allegations are called accusations, expert opinions are called opinions, and the closing names the specific documents that would change the story instead of a recap.

POLITICS MODE CAPTIONS AND DELIVERY: Excerpt captions are burned in from the curated quote text (script spelling, e.g. $5,000), sit in their own zone that cannot touch other graphics, and start a new cue at every speaker change; the SRT marks speaker changes. Narration uses the approved Cedar preset and every take's ending is verified by a second transcription because the model can drop a short final clause. Shorts end within a second of the last word, never padded to a round length. Deliver SCRIPT.md, FACT_CHECK.md (one row per claim with its source and treatment), SOURCE_MANIFEST.json, AUDIO_REPORT.json, QA_REPORT.json, UPLOAD_PACKAGE.md and headline thumbnails, and state plainly what was inspected by eye and what was only measured.

HOUSE GRAPHICS (every production, any subject): Render on-screen graphics with videoai_graphics.broadcast, the one house system for politics, science, gaming, sports and everything else; the subject only sets the accent colours. Bold condensed uppercase chyrons and tabs on solid bars, a white headline bar under the boxed footage that carries the quote text on excerpts and the chapter headline otherwise, a white sidebar card with a coloured header, big condensed numbers on a dark ground for full-screen figures, a channel wordmark block and chapter tag in the top band, and a footer strap. Footage is boxed with its own graphics intact and labelled with outlet, programme and date; excerpts get a speaker tab and an ORIGINAL AUDIO tab. Keep it crisp: export at the sources' native resolution, never upscale, keep text inside the safe areas, and burn captions into the white bar with word timing re-derived from the audio. Do not invent a different look per video; propose changes to the shared module instead.
